record.paper_title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions
record.original_question: Is the energy dependence of the eta-helium-3 interaction largely governed by the interaction of the eta meson with the deuteron substructure inside helium-3? This question is motivated by the observed similarity between eta-deuteron and eta-helium-3 interaction energy dependences when both are plotted using cross-section-derived final-state-interaction amplitudes.

evidence.quote: When plotted in the same figure both the ηd interaction and the η3He interaction show a very similar energy dependence.
This similarity might point at the conjecture used above, namely that the η3He dynamics is at least to a large extend given by the interaction of the η with the deuteron substructure of the He.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the strong interaction between an η meson and a light nucleus. For a near-threshold production reaction X → Y η on a target with final-state nucleus Y, one can extract an η–Y "final-state-interaction (FSI) amplitude" from the measured total cross section by dividing out the appropriate phase-space and primary-production factors, thereby isolating the energy dependence due to η–Y rescattering. Empirically, when this FSI amplitude is plotted as a function of the η center-of-mass momentum (or excess energy Q) for the η–d system (extracted, e.g., from pn → dη) and for the η–³He system (extracted, e.g., from dp → ³He η), the two curves exhibit a strikingly similar energy dependence near threshold, including a rapid rise consistent with a large η-nucleus scattering length.

Regarding ³He as a three-nucleon bound state with a significant deuteron-like (np) substructure plus a spectator proton, formulate and decide the following question:

Is the energy dependence of the η–³He interaction near threshold predominantly governed by the interaction of the η meson with the deuteron (np) substructure inside ³He? More precisely, does there exist a quantitative model in which the η–³He near-threshold scattering amplitude factorizes (up to a slowly varying spectator factor) through an η–d subamplitude in such a way that the observed coincidence of energy dependences of the η–d and η–³He FSI amplitudes is reproduced, and is this mechanism in fact the dominant one?
artifact.category_tag: Eta-nucleus interactions and few-body hadronic physics
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and experimental works on η³He near-threshold dynamics (including the search for η-mesic helium) continue to discuss the strong η³He final-state interaction and the role of the deuteron substructure, but no consensus quantitative derivation establishes that the η–³He energy dependence is dominantly due to η–d rescattering. The production mechanism remains characterized as "poorly understood," indicating the conjecture is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Status of the Search for η-Mesic Nuclei with Particular Focus on η-Helium Bound States
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews the strong η³He final-state interaction and ongoing search for η-mesic helium bound states; the production mechanism and underlying dynamics are still under investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The η³He near-threshold dynamics and bound-state interpretation remain active open questions.

status_evidence.title: Eta Meson Production in Proton-Deuteron Collisions (MESON 2014)
status_evidence.snippet: The pd → ³Heη reaction is motivated by anomalous near-threshold behavior and a poorly understood production mechanism, ascribed to a strong η³He final-state interaction.
status_evidence.claim: The microscopic origin of the strong η³He FSI, including the role of deuteron substructure, has not been definitively established.
